subject: Optimize pdf output size of geom_jitter

messages.author: 432b2470f0167457
messages.subject: Optimize pdf output size of geom_jitter
parts:
Hello there.

I have a dataset with about 25.000 entries. I want to print a geom_boxplot and a geom_jitter.

This is the minimal example:
> library(ggplot2)
> library(tikzDevice)
>
> # The plot
> data <- data.frame(amount = sample(1:100000,25000,replace=T))
>
> q <- ggplot(data)
> q <- q + aes(x = '', y = amount)
> q <- q + geom_jitter(alpha=1/8, color='red')
> q <- q + geom_boxplot(alpha=1/100, color='black', outlier.size = 1)
> q <- q + coord_flip()
> q
>
> # Tikz -> PDF Output
> tikz('sample_jitter.tex', standAlone=T, width=5.9, height=1.0, sanitize=F)
> print(q)
> dev.off()
> system("export PATH=/usr/texbin:$PATH; latexmk --pdf -pdflatex='lualatex' sample_jitter.tex; latexmk -c",int=T)


Now I'm running this threw the tikzdevice and render an pdf with lualatex, so I still have a vector based graphic. Usually this results in a pdf file about 2 MB big. Once I reduce the size in Acrobat Pro it is only about 200 kB big.

BUT: All PDF-Viewer I tried so far (Acrobat, Apple Preview and Skim) have quite some trouble rendering that pdf (takes seconds), because it countains so many points. It even get's worse, when trying to print this pdf (takes minutes if not longer).

So my main question is (even thou, this is more a pdf than a ggplot2 question): How can I feather optimize the output to improve printing time?

Converting this to a png or jpeg is not an options, since I want the text to be sharp.

Greetings from Berlin
Alex

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Optimize pdf output size of geom_jitter
parts:
Hi,

I have no practical suggestion to offer, but a wish for future
development of the package. Some geoms such as tile, or point, can
often result in really large vector files. A workaround for off-screen
rendering might be to add an optional .rasterize=FALSE parameter to
those layers. They would internally be converted to bitmaps (written
as a temporary file), and positioned as a layer in the final vector
output. I believe the tikzDevice developers have considered something
along those lines to implement the new raster graphic functions.

Just a thought,

baptiste

messages.author: 432b2470f0167457
messages.subject: Re: Optimize pdf output size of geom_jitter
parts:
Hello again.

The main problem doesn't seem to be the amount of points, but that every point contains alpha-information.

I helped myself with converting the pdf to a 600 dpi png file. Rendering and printing is much faster now. Especially the printing results look really good. The downside is, that the plot inside the latex document can look unsharp in the pdf viewer, depending on the zoom level (even 100% often looks quite unsharp).

For converting the pdf to png I use image magic and the following bash function:

function pdf_to_png600() {
jobname=`echo $@|sed 's/\.pdf$//g'`;
convert -density 600 -units pixelsperinch $jobname.pdf $jobname.png;
}

Now I just have to type 'pdf_to_png600 geom_plot.pdf' and a geom_plot.png file is created in the same directory.

I hope I can help some others with this, who experience the same .

Greetings from Berlin
Alex

messages.author: c9e805a6fe6dd903
messages.subject: Re: Optimize pdf output size of geom_jitter
parts:
you may be having a latex/tex issue rather than a ggplot issue. Have you considered the following?

You can speed up repeated calls to the tikzDevice by caching the tikz font metrics dictionary

I use the following:

options( tikzMetricsDictionary = "build/4tikzMetricsDictionary" )
where build is a temporary subdirectory

Also if you final image pat of a latex document, I would sugguest setting standalone to FALSE and including the generate tikz tex file directly using the latex \input command.

Alan
